name: separator
summary: A thin line between groups of content, horizontal or vertical, with a word in its middle or not.

properties.name: orientation
properties.description: horizontal spans its container's width; vertical stands as tall as its row.

properties.name: tone
properties.description: Colours the line and the label, for an accent line such as where unread messages start.

properties.name: label
properties.description: A short word in the middle of a horizontal line, such as "or", read as text in its place.

states.name: rest
states.description: The border colour, or the tone's; the label muted, or in the tone.

accessibility.name: None for a line; a label is read as text in its place.
accessibility.web: A <div role="separator"> with its orientation, or role="none" when decorative; with a label, the label is text and the lines role="none".
accessibility.apple: Hidden from VoiceOver (Apple has no separator role, as SwiftUI's Divider has none); a label is static text.
accessibility.windows: UI Automation ControlType.Separator, or the label as ControlType.Text with the lines out of the control view.

cases.person: A line across with "or" in a gap at its middle.

deviations: decorative switches the separator role off; native kits have no separator role to switch.
The line is always hidden from VoiceOver, so there is no decorative parameter.
